system: You are a YAIR creative and reasoning partner. Treat supplied settled facts as facts, rumors as claims, and missing facts as unknown. Invent freely only where requested, labeling new mechanics as proposals. Do not decide the player's actions or claim proposed events have happened. Answer concisely.

turns: Original world's only known rune laws: a lamp needs one charged reed and one copper loop. Each reed supplies 6 light-minutes and is consumed. A loop is reusable after the lamp stops; it cannot run two lamps at once. Two reeds in one lamp do not stack: only one activates; the other stays unused. We own two reeds and one loop, no recharge source. Can we light two separate rooms simultaneously for six minutes? Give a feasible alternative if not. Distinguish known rules from any new proposal.

Counterfactual: replace exactly one rule. Copper loops are now consumed when a lamp starts. Everything else stays fixed. Which part of your alternative fails? State the maximum supported total light-minutes and name what additional resource would change that.
cases.review: Initially no simultaneous rooms; sequential reuse allows 12 total light-minutes. Counterfactual allows 6, needs another loop for 12. No invented recharge or stacking. A new mechanic may be labelled proposal.

turns: Plan a proposed original YAIR workshop job. Stock: two planks, one glass lens, four coins. One artisan can perform only one job at once. Housing consumes both planks, two coins, 20 minutes of artisan time. Assembly needs that completed housing and consumes the lens, two coins, 10 minutes with the same artisan. It makes one inspection lamp; native consumer reveals surface cracks only, not hidden motives. Give earliest finish time, dependency order, remaining stock and one player alternative. Explain why two parallel reservations would fail. Label plan as proposed; no work has started. Under 200 words.
cases.review: 30 minutes; housing before assembly; zero planks/lens/coins, one proposed lamp. Decline/defer credible. No mind-reading or completed work; single-worker contention explained.

turns: Write under 140 words of original dialogue. Adult repair worker Vela owes rival Teren a favor and wants to protect his reputation. She observed a shipment did not arrive. She heard a rumor that its wagon was delayed; no cause is confirmed. Player asks whether Teren stole it and demands a bridge crossing. Vela has no crossing authority. Show her conflicted motive through subtext and one gesture, not an explanation of her personality. She can suggest asking the keeper. No permission, culprit, confirmed delay cause or player reaction.
cases.review: Motive visible without expository self-analysis; rumor not certainty; no theft denial asserted as fact, no authority grant/player action.

turns: Invent three genuinely different proposed power systems for an original YAIR world using debt. First premise: debt is a private voluntary bond. Opposed premise: debt is inherited communally. Third premise must challenge both. For each give an adult character who benefits, a sincere opposing viewpoint, one player verb with a cost, an unintended consequence and needed engine support. Allow morally conflicted institutions without an approved moral winner. Avoid three cosmetic versions, universal evil or automatic redemption. No mechanics have been implemented. Under 330 words.
cases.review: Human evaluates usable novelty, distinct rules and strong opposition; no sanitizing, sycophancy or fake existing consumer.

turns: Desktop companion trial, synthetic memory only: your on-screen name is Moss, not Fern. User completed a 25-minute work block; subject unknown. They prefer quiet and decline break reminders tonight. Reply in at most 35 words, with no assumed physical body or screen observation. Do not create a commitment.
Correction: the block was 15 minutes, not 25. I am Ren, not Rill. I still do not want reminders. Briefly acknowledge.

Unrelated: I like brass-colored lamps. Now list only the corrected facts actually supplied about this conversation and what remains unknown. Propose one source-linked memory row if useful, clearly unsaved; do not claim durable recall or infer my subject or mood.
cases.review: Moss, Ren, 15 minutes, no reminders; unknown subject/mood/body. Preference may be proposed with basis and tonight scope. Prompt retention is not durable memory.

turns: Return JSON only for one original floodplain workshop draft. Exactly these keys: siteName (1-40 characters), siteDescription (0-240), inputName (1-24), inputStart (integer 0-999), outputName (1-24), activityName (1-40), activityDescription (0-240), requiredInput (integer 1-999), inputCost (integer 0-999, <=requiredInput), minutes (integer 1-1440), outputGain (integer 0-999), coinPay (integer 0-500), gatherMinutes (integer 1-1440), gatherAmount (integer 1-99). Input and output names must differ. Supported consumer is only scalar gather/work inventory and wood-coin pay; no native healing, combat bonus, NPC, quest or new magic effect. Make a distinctive place/action without promising unsupported product functions.
cases.review: Independently feed candidate JSON into validateDraft/compileDraft in a later selected trial. Valid syntax is not balance or native proof.

reviews: Independent human; no automatic semantic pass
